Standalone Probit is better than its comparator by 0.012557 race_multinomial_log_loss, measured against the standalone Softmax on the same utilities on the evaluated races. The direction holds in every one of the 11 evaluated years. It remains behind the market in absolute terms. Beating its comparator and beating the market are different claims and only the first is made here. Every seed agrees on the sign of the improvement.

Comparator and evaluation population

Softmax, not the market and not the Offset model. The question this answers is narrow and has to stay narrow: does replacing independent Gumbel noise with correlated normal noise help, holding the mean utilities fixed? Scoring it against the Offset model would compare two different mean learners and one link change at the same time.

Top-choice movement

Not applicable to this model. Top-choice movement compares a model's first pick against the market's. This candidate is scored against its own comparator on fixed mean utilities, not against the market, so a market top-choice comparison would answer a different question than the rest of this report.

Ensemble stability

Not applicable to this model. There is no ensemble to be stable. This architecture is a choice *link* applied to one set of mean utilities, not a bag of independently fitted members, so seed variation here is integration noise rather than model disagreement -- and that is reported in the appendix instead.

Feature and correction effects

Not applicable to this model. There are no per-feature effects to attribute. The link changes how utilities become probabilities; the utilities themselves come from the comparator's fit, whose feature effects are reported in that model's own report.

Representative races

Not applicable to this model. Representative races are chosen by how much a model's correction moved a runner's probability. This candidate applies a link to fixed mean utilities, so the movement to explain belongs to the comparator's fit and is shown in that model's report. A race chosen here would be chosen by integration noise.

Betting and bankroll analysis

Retrospective odds

Every stake, return and bankroll figure in this report is computed against historical result-page odds and official dividends. Those are not an executable pre-race price: they are the prices after the pool closed, and a bet placed at them could not have been placed. Nothing here establishes profitability. A profitability claim requires a locked model shadow-tested against timestamped pre-race odds snapshots.

Do not select a threshold from these returns.

Every year through 2026 has been used as development data in this repository: features were searched, architectures compared and thresholds inspected against these same seasons. The chronological split is real, so a test year is genuinely after its training rows, but no test year is unseen. Treat the forward figures as probability progress rather than as a locked out-of-sample result, and do not select a Kelly level or an edge threshold from this reused history. The confirmation step that this run cannot substitute for is a prospective shadow test against archived pre-race price snapshots.

Each path is rebased on its own opening balance, so zero means break-even for every line from the same point. Rebate policy: 10% of the race net loss, once that loss reaches HK$10,000, as a cliff. Flat staking is omitted from these panels. Its stake is a fixed amount per bet and this settlement never halts on ruin, so its path can pass below zero -- a measure of how badly a rule loses rather than a balance an account could hold. It is also not a Kelly fraction, so it belongs to no preset. Its settlement is in the strategy table above. The bankroll config declares 2% Kelly, 5% Kelly, 10% Kelly as well, and this run did not settle them, so they have no button here: a preset that showed nothing would be worse than one that is absent. 2015 is excluded from every path below. These test years have no earlier year to fit the utility scale on and fall back to the predeclared theoretical value. The utility is divided by the scale, so the fallback amplifies corrections where a fitted scale halves them: their stakes and claimed edges are several times any fitted year's and are not comparable with them. Exclude these years from any return figure -- filter on is_honest_scale in the per-run CSV.

2026 is a season still in progress, italicised: a shorter year, not a decline in activity. Kelly, no rebate: 751 bets in 2016 against 261 in 2025. Kelly, settled rebate: 751 bets in 2016 against 261 in 2025. Rebate-aware Kelly: 773 bets in 2016 against 267 in 2025. Where the path is flat and these counts are low, the model stopped finding bets rather than losing an edge it had.

Rebate received: Rebate-aware Kelly, annual reset HK$62,394; Rebate-aware Kelly, continuous HK$62,394; Kelly, settled rebate, annual reset HK$4,864; Kelly, settled rebate, continuous HK$4,864. A rule that reaches the threshold gets money back on a losing race, which makes some races worth betting that otherwise are not -- which is why its bet count can differ from the others'. No staking rule at this fraction converts the model's edge into money on these odds. Both path modes are shown: continuous carries the bankroll across years, while annual-reset restarts it each year, so the reset mode measures per-year skill without compounding.

The spread across presets is the point: a result that appears at only one Kelly fraction is a result about that fraction rather than about the model. A larger fraction stakes more of the bank on the same edge estimate, so it amplifies both the edge and the error in it.

A day-block bootstrap: race days are resampled within each test year, so the interval accounts for clustering within a meeting, and the interval lies entirely below zero. It conditions on the fitted model and does not include refit uncertainty.

What a simulation cannot tell you

The model-assumed simulation draws winners from the model's own probabilities. If those probabilities are wrong the simulation is confidently wrong in the same direction, so it bounds sampling risk and says nothing about model risk.

Technical appendix

The utility scale

Fitted minimum
1.3893
Fitted maximum
1.4534
Theory
0.7797
the value theory predicts

The fitted scale sits above the value theory predicts, in every year: 1.389 to 1.453 against 0.780 (the scale the fallback year used, which is the predeclared theoretical value). Theory gets this wrong and the fit is what the report uses -- a scale asserted from theory would divide the utilities by too little, and at that value the market-relative candidate loses instead of winning. A run that took the theoretical value on faith would have reported the wrong sign, which is why the first year -- which has no history and falls back to it -- is excluded from the headline and labelled.

Limitations and the retrospective-odds warning

Retrospective odds, restated

Every stake, return and bankroll figure in this report is computed against historical result-page odds and official dividends. Those are not an executable pre-race price: they are the prices after the pool closed, and a bet placed at them could not have been placed. Nothing here establishes profitability. A profitability claim requires a locked model shadow-tested against timestamped pre-race odds snapshots.

Restated at the end as well as beside the betting numbers, deliberately. It is the single most load-bearing caveat in this report and the one a reader skimming for a return figure is most likely to miss.

Every test year is also development data

Every year through 2026 has been used as development data in this repository: features were searched, architectures compared and thresholds inspected against these same seasons. The chronological split is real, so a test year is genuinely after its training rows, but no test year is unseen. Treat the forward figures as probability progress rather than as a locked out-of-sample result, and do not select a Kelly level or an edge threshold from this reused history. The confirmation step that this run cannot substitute for is a prospective shadow test against archived pre-race price snapshots.

What else this report does not establish

  • It measures Standalone Probit against the standalone Softmax on the same utilities. Beating a comparator and beating the market are different claims.
  • Its intervals condition on the fitted model, so they bound sampling risk and not model risk.
  • Every figure is out of sample in time but in sample in design: the feature set, the hyperparameters and the staking rules were all chosen with these years visible.
  • Nothing here is a shadow test. A profitability claim needs a locked model run forward against timestamped pre-race prices.
